comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (Teaching and Examination Regulations), first cohort year of the fixed Fall 2026 comparison
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official Teaching and Examination Regulations (OER) 2026-2027 list ten compulsory 6-EC units of education in each of Year 1 and Year 2, plus a compulsory 12-EC Bachelor's thesis and three 6-EC 'Recap' units (Criminal Law, Private Law, Public Law) in Year 3, together with at least 30 EC of elective space in the first semester of Year 3 that a student fills with a VU minor, an Examination-Board-approved equivalent 30-EC package, or exchange credits. The 2025 NVAO accreditation report confirms the programme has no named specialisation or track ('Specialisations or tracks: -'), so no comparator route is selected. The elective minor space is preserved generically at its full 30 EC rather than filled with an invented minor package, since students choose it freely from an open catalogue of VU minors and exchange options. The programme's own marketing and curriculum pages organise the first two years around four recurring themes (security, globalisation of markets, migration, sustainability); those themes are used only to group the OER's compulsory units of education for comparison purposes and do not add or remove any credit-bearing component.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by doctrinal law (human rights, criminal, private, constitutional, EU and international law) integrated with political science, sociology, psychology, philosophy and negotiation; the combination label describes this multi-field legal/governance programme rather than treating one strand as the whole.

alternatives.concept: A business, economics and environmental-governance programme examining how law, regulation and corporate practice should respond to the globalisation of markets, the platform economy and climate/sustainability responsibility, reorganising the evidenced sustainability and globalisation-of-markets themes around business, economics and environmental-governance coursework rather than doctrinal law.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by business, economics and sustainability-governance courses (international business, public economics, econometrics, market research, marketing, sustainability essentials, governance of sustainability, applied sustainability research) with only a small doctrinal-law and human-rights anchor, so the sustainability/business/markets label accurately describes the completed programme rather than its law origin.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: This route replaces 15 of the 24 courses used in the closest-match programme (all of the criminal, constitutional and EU-law courses, political theory, peace & conflict, negotiation, philosophy, extremism and most social-science courses) with business, economics and environmental-governance coursework (international business and governance, public economics, econometrics, marketing, market research, sustainability essentials I/II, life-cycle analysis, applied sustainability research, and data science). It keeps only a minimal shared anchor (PPD, the transnational business-law course, the two business/research gateways, human-rights law, AI ethics, climate change and sustainability governance) and organises the whole curriculum around corporate and market accountability rather than around doctrinal criminal, constitutional and international law.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest-match programme covers the core law-and-justice field together with the security and international-governance stable directions (migration/refugee law and security/terrorism are substantively covered by its criminal, international and human-rights law content, since UCR offers no dedicated migration-law course). The sustainability/globalisation-of-markets direction is evidenced by two further stable study directions and three direct interests and organises a genuinely distinct 24-course business/economics/environmental-governance programme, differing from the closest match by 15 of 24 courses. Every generator-eligible interest row is now owned by one of these two programmes, leaving no remaining coherent, evidence-backed direction for a third alternative; production stops at two.

notes.text: Law in Society requires ten compulsory law/social-science units in each of Year 1 and Year 2, a 12-EC bachelor's thesis and three advanced 'Recap' law courses reviewing criminal, private and public law in Year 3. UCR's selected programmes can combine a comparable range of law, social-science and (in the second alternative) business/sustainability courses, but neither reproduces VU's dedicated migration-law course, its second criminal-law unit, or its compulsory bachelor's thesis; UCR's standardized Optional independent research element is offered instead of a required thesis.
